about: The built-in football seasons before FIFA 05 (docs/design/football-years.md, 'Seasons before FIFA 05'), built by npm run build:retro-seasons (scripts/build-retro-seasons.mjs) into public/football/<id>.json. Every source is pinned by SHA-256 and read from the gitignored data-src/<folder>/; download names where it came from, and a cd block the CD image npm run sync:retro-cds reads it from (scripts/sync-retro-cds.mjs). The data's rights stay with its makers (Sports Interactive and Eidos, Sensible Software and Codemasters, and three fans: Cam F, Simon Treanor and Alex Sawczuk), and every season is credited to them. The user chose to ship 2002/03, 2001/02, 1998/99, 1997/98 and 1996/97 (2026-11-08) and the two fan databases (2026-11-09), and Sawczuk's 2003/04 update on 2026-11-10; Claude added 2000/01, 1999/00, 1995/96 and 1994/95 on 2026-11-09 under the user's request to cover every missing season, and the user approved shipping them on 2026-11-10 after being told CM 00/01's and CM 99/00's data come from games never made free. A season's own `retrieved` overrides the manifest's where its sources were read another day.

seasons.listing: Alex Sawczuk's October 2003 update of SI's Championship Manager 01/02 database, fan-made (the Official Championship Manager Magazine's issue 5 cover CD, archive.org cmmag-05)
seasons.compiler: Alex Sawczuk's 'Sawczuk Update' (7th version, transfers to 26 October 2003, with German, Croatian, US and other data he credits to contributors), as the Official Championship Manager Magazine's issue 5 cover CD (Future Publishing, November 2003) carries it: its Data tables read by HTTP range from archive.org cmmag-05 (CMMag05.iso); club.dat and staff.dat are the files src/data/cm0102Releases.js pins for it
seasons.provenance: A fan's update of SI's CM 01/02 3.9.68 database (November 2002). For players kept under the same staff id and name, 98.6% of current abilities are still SI's 3.9.68 values (103,459 rated in both), so most ratings are a season old; the rest were changed by hand, above all in the Premier League, where 57% of players were re-rated, 8.2 points higher on average on the 1-200 scale, against 10-14% and +1.6 to +1.9 in Serie A, La Liga and the Bundesliga and 0.9% outside the seven leagues. English clubs so take 15 places of the Elite 32, where 3.9.68 gives them 7. 375 rated players are new. The squads are of October 2003: Beckham at Real Madrid, Ronaldinho at Barcelona, Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United, Duff, Crespo, Makelele and Verón at Chelsea. Its Eredivisie lists Excelsior (eight rated players) instead of FC Volendam, so it fields 17 clubs; its La Liga lists Real Oviedo, relegated in 2001, and puts Málaga in the second division; its Ligue 1 keeps CM 01/02's 18 clubs, so Ajaccio and Montpellier, in 2003/04's 20-club Ligue 1, play in its second division. Players who retired before the season keep their records with a current ability of 1 (Schmeichel, Bierhoff, Blanc); none of them is among the players written.
seasons.rights: A fan's update of SI's CM 01/02 3.9.68 data: SI's and Eidos's rights in the data it starts from, and the author's in his edits; it names no licence, and the official magazine distributed it on its cover disc. The archive.org item is a user's upload of that disc. The user chose to ship it on 2026-11-10 (docs/design/football-year-permissions.md). Only the eleven tables below are read from it.

seasons.listing: SI's Championship Manager 00/01 database, original release 3.81 (the UK retail CD's data files, archive.org cm-0001-rel)
seasons.compiler: SI's own data files from the retail CD's InstallShield cabinet (DATA1.CAB), read by HTTP range from archive.org cm-0001-rel (CM0001_rel.iso), each file's MD5 as the cabinet header records it
seasons.provenance: The CD's volume CM0001_rel was mastered on 6 October 2000, three weeks before the game's release on 27 October: the release-day database. A later European pressing (archive.org cm-0001) agrees on 96.3% of current abilities (39,382 players matched by name and date of birth) and rates 1,866 more players, with a few later transfers (Weah at Marseille rather than Manchester City); it is not the one read. The squads are of the summer of 2000: Figo at Real Madrid, Crespo at Lazio, Batistuta at Roma; Charlton, Manchester City and Ipswich promoted. Four players with a current ability below 0 are unrated and left out. For players matched by name and date of birth, 61.8% of current abilities equal CM 99/00's, which sit 2.6 lower on average (22,544 players, correlation 0.931), and 50.3% equal SI's CM 01/02 3.9.60's, which sit 0.7 higher (35,810 players, correlation 0.924): one scale, so the conversion is CM 01/02's, unchanged.
seasons.rights: Championship Manager: Season 00/01 is Sports Interactive's and Eidos's (now SEGA's and Square Enix's) and was never made free, unlike CM 01/02; the archive.org item is a user's upload of the retail CD, and the data's rights are reserved. Only the eleven tables below are read from it.

seasons.listing: SI's Championship Manager 99/00 database, original release 3.70 (the UK retail CD's data files, archive.org championship-manager-season-9900)
seasons.compiler: SI's own data files from the retail CD's InstallShield cabinet (DATA1.CAB), read by HTTP range from archive.org championship-manager-season-9900 (CM9900_REL.bin), each file's MD5 as the cabinet header records it
seasons.provenance: The CD's volume CM9900_REL was mastered on 16 November 1999; the game was released on 3 December 1999. A second copy, the Dutch CD (archive.org cm-9900-nl), carries a byte-identical cabinet header, so every data file's MD5 agrees. The squads are of the autumn of 1999: Vieri at Inter, Anelka at Real Madrid, Shevchenko at Milan; Bradford City, Watford and Sunderland promoted. It names the Eredivisie after its sponsor (Dutch KPN-Telecompetition) and spells Burkina Faso 'Burkino Faso'; both are read as such. For players matched by name and date of birth, 70.5% of current abilities equal the CM3 port's (1998/99), which sit 2.0 lower on average (15,637 players, correlation 0.947): the scale of the seasons around it, so the conversion is CM 01/02's, unchanged.
seasons.rights: Championship Manager: Season 99/00 is Sports Interactive's and Eidos's (now SEGA's and Square Enix's) and was never made free, unlike CM 01/02; the archive.org item is a user's upload of the retail CD (its Public Domain Mark does not apply to the game), and the data's rights are reserved. Only the eleven tables below are read from it.

seasons.listing: SI's Championship Manager 3 data in the CM 01/02 format, Cam F's port (the CM0102 Starter Kit's cm3_data.zip)
seasons.compiler: Cam F, "Season 98/99 for 0102 (CM3)" (champman0102.co.uk t=1547, 28 November 2020), converted by Gio about 2011; as nckstwrt's CM0102 Starter Kit ships it (data/cm3_data.zip, first commit 9 June 2021). Not Cam F's later rework to September 1998.

seasons.listing: SI's Championship Manager 97/98 database as baskeyx extracted it to JSON (github.com/baskeyx/cm9798)
seasons.compiler: baskeyx (Dan Baskey): the cm9798 package, extracted to JSON (commit 06bdd2b, 5 October 2026)
seasons.provenance: The extraction names neither the tool that read the game's files nor the game's version (2.81 or 2.93), and it holds Scandinavian, Japanese, Turkish and MLS divisions the UK release did not play, so it may come from another release or an edited database. No second copy of its values exists. Its transfers stop in September 1997: Ravanelli is at Marseille and Yeboah at Hamburg, Karembeu still at Sampdoria, Klinsmann at Sampdoria and Davids at Milan. For the same players its abilities run about 9 points above the next season's on the 1-200 scale (110.9 against 101.4 in the CM3 port for 7,435 players matched by name and nation, correlation 0.69, 27% identical; 9.5 above SI's 3.9.60), so its ratings sit about 4.7 higher across the board; the conversion is CM 01/02's, unchanged.
seasons.rights: The package's code is MIT; its player and team data, extracted from the game, is not, and its rights stay with Sports Interactive and Eidos.

seasons.listing: Sensible Software's Sensible World of Soccer 96/97 national squads (Whiteulver's database, as keyser1884's SWOS-MCP holds it)
seasons.compiler: Whiteulver's database of the game's teams, xflea's spreadsheet of it (v1.1, December 2018), as keyser1884's SWOS-MCP holds it (swos_database.db, commit ac15d74, 9 July 2025)
seasons.provenance: Row for row the spreadsheet; its Swedish club records equal the game's own team file (304 of 304 players), and its national squads gazchap's database (64 of 64 checked). A SWOS United thread (2021) says some minor nations' squads and nationalities in the game predate 1996.
seasons.rights: Sensible World of Soccer is Sensible Software's, published by Renegade and GT Interactive and now Codemasters'; the database's code is MIT, the game's data is not.

seasons.listing: Sensible Software's Sensible World of Soccer 95/96, its national squads and the seven leagues' top-division clubs (the game's own team files, as the SWOS United server keeps them)
seasons.compiler: The game's own team files: the six national team files (TEAM.080 to 085) and the seven league files (TEAM.008 England, 013 France, 014 Germany, 020 Italy, 025 Holland, 029 Portugal, 035 Spain), as the SWOS United community server keeps them for its tools (cern.swos.eu/data/amiga/9596), read by scripts/lib/swos-files.mjs
seasons.provenance: The launch edition of SWOS 95/96 (the server's 9596), not its European Championship Edition (9596ece, spring 1996, in which 585 of the 2,272 national players differ). Read the same way, SWOS 96/97's own files agree with the shipped 96/97 database for 1,441 of its 1,463 national players; the other 22 are that database's price step 0 stored as 25K, Maldini's and Shearer's step 49 stored as 15M, and namesakes. So steps are read as that database stores them: 0 as 1 (25K) and 49 as 48 (15M).
seasons.rights: Sensible World of Soccer is Sensible Software's; its rights are now Codemasters'. The SWOS United server, which keeps the game's files for its tools, states no licence or terms (it has no robots.txt), and the data's rights are reserved.

seasons.listing: Sensible Software's original Sensible World of Soccer (1994), its national squads and the seven leagues' top-division clubs (the game's own team files, as the SWOS United server keeps them)
seasons.compiler: The game's own team files: the six national team files (TEAM.080 to 085) and the seven league files (TEAM.008 England, 013 France, 014 Germany, 020 Italy, 025 Holland, 029 Portugal, 035 Spain), as the SWOS United community server keeps them for its tools (cern.swos.eu/data/amiga/v1.0), read by scripts/lib/swos-files.mjs
seasons.provenance: The original release, v1.0, whose READ.ME is Sensible Software's note of Christmas 1994 (kept beside the files in data-src). The v1.1 update of early 1995 has the same national teams and later club squads; the v0.9 pre-release has no Uruguay. Read the same way, SWOS 96/97's own files agree with the shipped 96/97 database for 1,441 of its 1,463 national players; the other 22 are that database's price step 0 stored as 25K, Maldini's and Shearer's step 49 stored as 15M, and namesakes. So steps are read as that database stores them: 0 as 1 (25K) and 49 as 48 (15M). Roberto Baggio's and Romário's step 49 is read as 48.
seasons.rights: Sensible World of Soccer is Sensible Software's; its rights are now Codemasters'. The SWOS United server, which keeps the game's files for its tools, states no licence or terms (it has no robots.txt), and the data's rights are reserved.

seasons.listing: Cam F's fan-made 1993/94 database for CM 01/02, its ratings Cam F's (the CM0102 Starter Kit's cm93_data.zip)
seasons.compiler: Cam F, "Season 93/94 For 0102" (champman0102.co.uk t=1546, 28 November 2020), a fan-made database in the CM 01/02 format; as nckstwrt's CM0102 Starter Kit ships it (data/cm93_data.zip, whose loader starts the game in 1993)
seasons.provenance: Fan-made: its players' abilities are Cam F's, not Sports Interactive's. Against SI's own CM 93/94 data (ben-clarke/championship-manager-93-tools' export) for 1,452 English-league players matched by name they correlate 0.72, 74 are equal, and Cam F's run 19 lower on average. It keeps CM 01/02's league sizes, not 1993/94's: its Premier Division has 20 clubs (Oldham Athletic and Swindon Town, of the real 22, are in its First Division) and its French First Division 18 (Angers and Martigues are in its Second), against 1993-94 FA Premier League and 1993-94 French Division 1 on Wikipedia (revisions 1371793527 and 1366136574).
seasons.rights: A fan-made database for CM 01/02, which Eidos made free to download in December 2008 for personal, non-commercial use; it names no licence. Its players and ratings are its maker's and the game's data rights are reserved; the user chose to ship it, credited to Cam F (2026-11-09).

seasons.listing: Simon Treanor's fan-made 1989/90 database for CM 01/02, Beta 5, its ratings his, nations only (the CM0102 Starter Kit's cm89_data.zip)
seasons.compiler: Simon Treanor, "Championship Manager 1989/90 update for CM 01/02", Beta 5 of 8 April 2017 (its readme; cm8990.wordpress.com), a fan-made database in the CM 01/02 format; as nckstwrt's CM0102 Starter Kit ships it (data/cm89_data.zip, whose loader starts the game in 1989)
seasons.provenance: Fan-made: its players' abilities are Simon Treanor's. Its readme calls it a beta in which many teams keep squads of the early 2000s, and names the English, Scottish, German and Italian leagues as complete. Its nationalities are today's (Ukraine, Croatia, Slovakia, East Germans as 'Germany'), so the season plays the federations of 1989/90: the Soviet Union, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia field their republics' players, and a 'Germany' player at an East German club plays for no nation (noNationAt). Nations only: its Spanish and Portuguese first divisions are 1989/90's (1989-90 La Liga and 1989-90 Primeira Divisão on Wikipedia, revisions 1337764526 and 1374234667), but Logroñés (7 rated players), Castellón and Tenerife (10 each) and eight of Portugal's eighteen (Chaves, Feirense, Marítimo, Nacional, Penafiel, Portimonense, Tirsense, União da Madeira) cannot field eleven.
seasons.rights: A fan-made database for CM 01/02, which Eidos made free to download in December 2008 for personal, non-commercial use; it names no licence. Its players and ratings are its maker's and the game's data rights are reserved; the user chose to ship it, credited to Simon Treanor (2026-11-09).

noNationAt.label: East German clubs
noNationAt.rule: The database's German clubs with a rated 'Germany' player whose stadium's city (its own stadium and city records) GeoNames' cities1000 places only in the five eastern states, or that scripts/lib/east-german-clubs.mjs lists by hand (East Berlin's, and towns the gazetteer names twice or not at all).
